issues.reason: The bare-kinds trigger does fire on "Trees use photosynthesis", so the routing observation stands; the defect half does not — the opaque kind relation has no event witness for the purpose infinitive's `(To …)` atom (the reviewer's own gap), and the distributing rule asserts nothing false, since every tree does use photosynthesis.

`carbon_dioxide` is a modifier_noun compound whose last word is a real head noun, and Compound concepts states the genus is "always emitted either way"; its absence also makes two faithful parses differ.

The "never mint a separate entity" bar is scoped to the subject-identity change of kind ("the museum IS the room"); here three consumed reactants yield a new substance, and the stated shape would force the false flat atoms `(Member sunlight sugar)` — so the product-entity `Result` is graceful improvisation in gap territory, every atom true and well-typed.

gaps_confirmed: a bare relational generic carrying further modifiers (here a purpose infinitive): the opaque kind relation has no event witness to anchor `(To <main> <purpose>)`, so the two prescribed forms cannot both be satisfied

many-to-one material transformation "turn A, B and C into D": the change-of-kind shape reifies the result state on the changed object's own symbol, which is undefined when several distinct objects yield one new substance

collective/aggregate reading of a coordinated OBJECT: coordination is distributive by default (false here — sunlight alone does not become sugar) and the collective one-event form is defined only for multiple `Agent` atoms, so stacked `Patient` atoms have no explicit licence
repair_summary: Added the mandatory compound-kind genus `(Inheritance carbon_dioxide dioxide)`; the rule itself is unchanged.
notes: The two refuted/partial issues are the same gap seen twice — the relational-generic and change-of-kind shapes are both unusable once the sentence adds a purpose clause and a many-to-one transformation, and the parser's improvisation keeps every atom true.
